assessments.reasoning: The Fifth Edition grammar distinguishes a sequence from a choice. Its accompanying normative rule requires matches to follow sequence order, with occurrence operators determining how often a particle or group can match. This controls validity against the declared element-content model.

challenge.method: Apply the rule to (a?,b) and (a,b)* to test omission and group repetition.
challenge.results: A lone b can match the first model. Repeated a,b pairs can match the second, including an a after a previous pair's b. Each group occurrence still obeys its declared order.

limitations: Occurrence modifiers and choices govern which occurrences match. This is a DTD validity rule scoped to a sequence model.
The claim does not impose a sequence on every XML element or require an independent optional particle to occur.
